title: Present Simple
question_text: Choose the correct form: She ___ to school every day.
explanation: Use -s with he/she/it in the present simple.

title: Present Simple
question_text: Choose the correct form: They ___ football on Saturdays.
explanation: Use the base form with they.

title: Present Simple
question_text: Choose the correct form: He ___ coffee every morning.
explanation: Use -s with he/she/it.

title: Present Simple
question_text: Choose the correct form: We ___ TV in the evening.
explanation: Use the base form with we.

title: Present Simple
question_text: Choose the correct form: The dog ___ a lot.
explanation: Use -s with singular subjects.

title: Present Simple
question_text: Choose the correct form: I ___ to music after dinner.
explanation: Use the base form with I.

title: Present Simple
question_text: Choose the correct form: She ___ her homework every day.
explanation: Use -s with she.

title: Be: am/is/are
question_text: I ___ a student.
explanation: Use am with I.

title: Articles
question_text: I have ___ apple.
explanation: Use an before a vowel sound.

title: Articles
question_text: This row is intentionally missing an explanation.
explanation: The correct answer is "a".

title: Plural Nouns
question_text: There are two ___ on the table.
explanation: Most regular nouns take -s in the plural.

title: There is / There are
question_text: ___ three chairs in the room.
explanation: Use There are with plural nouns.

title: Can
question_text: I ___ swim.
explanation: Can is followed by the base form of the verb.

title: Past Simple
question_text: Yesterday, I ___ at home.
explanation: Use the past simple for a finished past action.

title: Possessive Adjectives
question_text: This is ___ book. I own it.
explanation: My comes before a noun.

title: Prepositions
question_text: The keys are ___ the table.
explanation: Use on for a surface.

title: Question Words
question_text: ___ is your name?
explanation: What asks for information about a thing or name.

title: Irregular Verbs
question_text: True or false: 'I goed to the store' is grammatically correct.
explanation: 'Go' is irregular; the past tense is 'went', not 'goed'.

title: Irregular Verbs
question_text: Choose the correct past form: She ___ to Paris last year.
explanation: Went is the irregular past tense of go.

title: Irregular Verbs
question_text: Choose the correct past form: He ___ his keys yesterday.
explanation: Lost is the irregular past tense of lose.

title: Irregular Verbs
question_text: Choose the correct past form: They ___ the cake at the party.
explanation: Ate is the irregular past tense of eat.

title: Irregular Verbs
question_text: Choose the correct past form: I ___ a great book last week.
explanation: Read (past tense) is spelled the same as the present but pronounced differently.

title: Comparative Adjectives
question_text: A car is ___ than a bicycle.
explanation: Use the comparative form faster for a two-item comparison.

title: Present Continuous
question_text: Look! The baby ___.
explanation: Use am/is/are + -ing for an action happening now.

title: Past Continuous
question_text: At 8 p.m., I ___ dinner.
explanation: Use was/were + -ing for an action in progress at a past time.

title: Future: going to
question_text: We ___ visit next weekend.
explanation: Use be + going to + base verb for plans.

title: First Conditional
question_text: If it rains, we ___ at home.
explanation: The first conditional uses if + present, then will + base verb.

title: Countable/Uncountable
question_text: How ___ water do you need?
explanation: Use much with uncountable nouns.

title: Adverbs of Frequency
question_text: She ___ gets up early; almost every day.
explanation: Usually means something happens often but not always.

title: Modal: should
question_text: You ___ see a doctor if you feel very ill.
explanation: Should is followed by the base verb.

title: Present Perfect
question_text: I ___ my homework already.
explanation: Use have/has + past participle for a completed action connected to now.

title: Too / Enough
question_text: This box is ___ heavy for me to carry.
explanation: Too + adjective means more than is wanted or possible.

title: Synonyms
question_text: Choose the closest synonym for 'happy'.
explanation: Glad is a close synonym of happy.

title: Synonyms
question_text: Choose the closest synonym for 'big'.
explanation: Large is a close synonym of big.

title: Synonyms
question_text: Choose the closest synonym for 'fast'.
explanation: Quick is a close synonym of fast.

title: Synonyms
question_text: Choose the closest synonym for 'smart'.
explanation: Clever is a close synonym of smart.

title: Synonyms
question_text: Choose the closest synonym for 'sad'.
explanation: Unhappy is a close synonym of sad.

title: Present Perfect vs Past Simple
description: Practice Present Perfect vs Past Simple.
question_text: I ___ London twice, but I first went there in 2022.
explanation: Use present perfect for life experience without a finished past time.

title: Second Conditional
question_text: If I had more time, I ___ another language.
explanation: Use if + past, would + base verb for hypothetical situations.

title: Relative Clauses
question_text: The woman ___ lives next door is a doctor.
explanation: Use who for people.

title: Reported Speech
question_text: He said that he ___ tired.
explanation: Backshift is commonly used when reporting a past statement.

title: Gerunds and Infinitives
question_text: She enjoys ___ books.
explanation: Enjoy is followed by a gerund (-ing form).

title: Modal Deduction
question_text: The lights are off. They ___ be at home.
explanation: Can't expresses a strong negative deduction.

title: Passive Voice
question_text: The bridge ___ in 1990.
explanation: The past passive uses was/were + past participle.

title: Linkers
question_text: I was tired; ___, I finished the report.
explanation: However introduces a contrast.

title: Used to
question_text: I ___ play football every weekend when I was younger.
explanation: Used to describes past habits or states.

title: Phrasal Verbs
question_text: Please ___ the lights before you leave.
explanation: Turn off means switch something off.

title: Word Order
question_text: Put the words in order: yesterday / to / went / I / the / market /.
explanation: Standard SVO order places the time expression at the end.
answer_1: I went to the market yesterday.
answer_2: Yesterday market the to went I.
answer_3: I to the market went yesterday.
answer_4: Went I yesterday to the market.

title: Word Order
question_text: Which word order is correct for a yes/no question?
explanation: Auxiliary verbs invert with the subject in questions.

title: Word Order
question_text: Which sentence has correct adjective order?
explanation: English adjective order is opinion-size-age-shape-color-origin-material-purpose.
answer_1: A beautiful small old round black wooden box.
answer_2: A wooden black round old small beautiful box.
answer_3: A box beautiful small old round black wooden.

title: Word Order
question_text: Which sentence places the adverb correctly?
explanation: Adverbs of frequency usually go before the main verb.
answer_2: I am always late for work not.

title: Word Order
question_text: Choose the sentence with the correct word order among all nine options.
explanation: Only option 9 follows correct subject-verb-object order.
answer_1: Market I yesterday went to the.
answer_2: To the market yesterday I went.
answer_3: Yesterday I the market to went.
answer_4: Went to market the I yesterday.
answer_5: The market yesterday to I went.
answer_6: I market the yesterday went to.
answer_7: To market the I went yesterday.
answer_8: Market to the yesterday went I.
answer_9: I went to the market yesterday.

title: Word Order
question_text: Which question word order is correct?
explanation: Wh-question word order is question word + auxiliary + subject + verb.

title: Mixed Conditionals
question_text: If I had studied harder, I ___ more confident now.
explanation: A past condition can have a present result.

title: Inversion
question_text: Rarely ___ such a beautiful performance.
explanation: Restrictive adverbs at the front can trigger inversion.

title: Modal Perfect
question_text: She ___ have forgotten the meeting; she never misses one.
explanation: Can't have + past participle expresses a strong negative deduction.

title: Causative
question_text: I had my car ___ yesterday.
explanation: Have + object + past participle describes a service arranged for someone.

title: Participle Clauses
question_text: ___ the report, she sent it to the manager.
explanation: Having + past participle shows the first action happened before the second.

title: Advanced Passive
question_text: The suspect is believed ___ abroad.
explanation: Is believed + to have + past participle reports an earlier action.

title: Hedging
question_text: The results ___ suggest that the policy was effective.
explanation: Appear to is a cautious way to state a conclusion.

title: Collocation
question_text: The company needs to ___ a decision quickly.
explanation: Make a decision is the standard collocation.

title: Concession
question_text: ___ the heavy traffic, we arrived on time.
explanation: Despite is followed by a noun phrase or gerund.

title: Register
question_text: Which is most appropriate in a formal report?
explanation: Formal reports favor precise, neutral vocabulary.

title: Advanced Conditionals
question_text: Had I known about the delay, I ___ earlier.
explanation: Had I known is an inverted third conditional.

title: Subjunctive
question_text: It is essential that every applicant ___ the form.
explanation: Formal English may use the base form after essential that.

title: Cleft Sentences
question_text: ___ I object to is the lack of evidence.
explanation: What I object to is a cleft construction.

title: Discourse Markers
question_text: The proposal is ambitious. ___, it is financially realistic.
explanation: Nevertheless signals contrast.

title: Nominalisation
question_text: The committee decided to delay the vote. The ___ was unexpected.
explanation: Decision is the noun form of decide.

title: Ellipsis
question_text: I can finish the report, and she can ___ too.
explanation: The repeated main verb can be retained or omitted after a modal; finish is the natural completion.

title: Lexical Precision
question_text: The evidence was ___; it supported several interpretations.
explanation: Ambiguous means open to more than one interpretation.

title: Inversion after Only
question_text: Only after the meeting ___ the implications become clear.
explanation: Only + fronted adverbial can require inversion.

title: Academic Stance
question_text: The findings ___ indicate a relationship between the variables.
explanation: Appear to indicates cautious academic interpretation.

title: Collocation
question_text: The report draws ___ attention to a serious gap.
explanation: Draw sharp attention to is a natural formal collocation.

title: Nuanced Modality
question_text: He ___ have been aware of the risk, but the evidence is inconclusive.
explanation: May have been expresses a possible past state.

title: Concessive Inversion
question_text: Much as I ___ the argument, I cannot accept the conclusion.
explanation: Much as + verb introduces a strong concession.

title: Fronting
question_text: What the report fails to explain ___ why the figures changed.
explanation: The subject is a singular noun clause, so use is.

title: Register and Tone
question_text: Which phrase is most suitable for a highly formal academic paper?
explanation: A substantial proportion of is formal and precise.

title: Semantic Nuance
question_text: The minister's response was deliberately ___, avoiding a direct commitment.
explanation: Equivocal means deliberately unclear or open to more than one interpretation.

title: Advanced Relative Construction
question_text: The proposal, ___ merits were debated for months, was finally rejected.
explanation: Whose can express possession in a non-defining relative clause.

title: Inversion with Negative Adverbial
question_text: Under no circumstances ___ the data be altered.
explanation: Negative fronted adverbials trigger inversion.

title: Pragmatics
question_text: Her 'That's interesting' was probably ___ given her dismissive tone.
explanation: Tone and context can make a seemingly positive phrase sarcastic.

title: Idiomatic Precision
question_text: The new evidence ___ serious doubt on the original claim.
explanation: Cast doubt on is the standard collocation.

title: Synthesis
question_text: Taken together, the findings ___ a more complex picture than the initial hypothesis suggested.
explanation: Paint a picture is a common metaphorical collocation in analytical writing.
